audit.whatIsWrong: 'Twofold Hunt' is not an Aurora ability, and the full layer uses it as her escape/blink in 21 strings. Her real Q is Twofold Hex (900 range, 9s at rank 1) — a curse missile with a recast that draws the curses back — and it is not a blink at all. The blink is Across the Veil (W, 22/21/20/19/18s), a leap that leaves her invisible with bonus Move Speed on landing.
audit.why: The whole full layer told the player to track the wrong ability under a made-up name. Naming the real escape and its 22s rank-1 cooldown makes 'engage when it is down' an actionable timer instead of a slogan, and the invisibility on landing explains why a chased Lunge whiffs.
audit.corrected: Every 'Twofold Hunt' / 'Twofold Hunt (Blink)' replaced with Across the Veil; its cooldown and the landing invisibility written into report[5].t, breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d; Twofold Hex's real range and cooldown written into dontsFull[0].d; Between Worlds' slow field and cross-field teleport written into dontsFull[2].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 1, 2 and 3 disagree with the packet and with their own explanations. Both layers print Aurora / Skill / Fiora; the packet reads Fiora / Fiora / Skill. whys[0] says 'own the lane and farm freely while she hides' — that is a Fiora row, printed as Aurora at 3/10. whys[1] says 'her single poke can't trade with that burst' — Fiora, printed as Skill. whys[2] says 'genuinely even until you bait the cooldown out' — Skill, printed as Fiora.
audit.why: The level-1 row was telling the player they lose 3/10 to one of the weakest melee-range level 1s in the game, directly under text saying the lane is free.
audit.corrected: Rows set to Fiora 7 / Fiora 7 / Skill 5 in both layers, with phases[0..2].why rewritten to state the new side and name Across the Veil's cooldown as the thing that flips row 3.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why claims Grand Challenge 'wins any committed duel' on the one row the packet, win[4] and whys[4] all give to Aurora.
audit.why: Level 6 is her window, not yours: Across the Veil displaces you out of the gap-close and Between Worlds (140s at rank 1) slows and bursts from range exactly as you commit. Telling the player their ult wins any duel on that row is the mistake the row exists to warn against.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now names both her abilities and the 140s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] tells the player 'parry the immobilize and the return becomes a stun' as though the stun were automatic.
audit.why: Riot's Riposte text is explicit that the stab slows the first champion hit, and stuns ONLY if Fiora blocked an immobilizing effect with that cast. Presenting the stun as guaranteed makes players hold a 24s cooldown for a payoff that usually does not arrive. The mirror audit reached the same conclusion from Aurora's side.
audit.corrected: wants.you[1] now states the condition and what you actually get when it is not met.

notes: Second fabricated-name matchup in a row: 'Twofold Hunt' appeared in 21 full-layer strings as Aurora's blink. Her Q is Twofold Hex (a curse missile, not a blink) and the blink is Across the Veil (W). All replaced. I left the content layer's repeated claim that her Q applies a ROOT completely untouched — Riot's Twofold Hex description says only that it curses enemies and can be recast to draw the curses back, with no immobilize mentioned, and the kit flags no hardCC on her Q. I could not verify it either way from the kits, so per the rules I did not write it and did not delete it. It is the load-bearing premise of early, wants.you[1] (original), spikes[3].text and late, so it is worth a hand check. I did correct the separate, verifiable error that Riposte's stun is automatic — Riot's text makes it conditional on parrying an immobilizing effect. Also note diff is 'TRICKY' at 7.5/10 against a 54.77% win rate over 398 games and a chart that is now five Fiora rows out of seven; I left diff, tone and diffRating alone rather than pick a rating token I could not confirm was valid.
